anchor.quote: Fix a prime $q$ (on this page $q$ is a prime, not a sequence length)
let $b\ge1$ be the number of base-$q$ digits of a field
Put $Q=q^b$, the number of values a field can take
let $V$ be the array volume, the number of stored data bits
where $a\in[Q]$ is the offset, prepared from the control values
Let $c$ be a fixed positive integer prime to $q$.
then produce output coordinates $y'=0,\dots,Q-1$ in order
A rational unit is a signed ratio $c/c'$ of positive integers $c,c'$ both prime to $q$.

gaps.term: inverse scaling by exchanging split and merge
gaps.quote: Exchanging split and merge multiplies by $c^{-1}$ (cited)
gaps.note: The page never says what the exchanged split and merge are for the inverse map, or why the swap gives multiplication by c^{-1}. The scaling construction splits by j and merges by a residue condition mod c, so the reader cannot tell what the swap means (split by residue class, merge by j). This stands in for how the inverse scaling works, and the later claim that the inverse of a unit costs O(V) depends on it. Paper line 604 says only that reversing the roles of split and merge implements multiplication by c^{-1}.
